method.model: STRIDE-informed trust-boundary review plus privacy data-flow and dependency inspection
limitations: This is an engineering review, not ENG-15 independent verification.
cargo-audit was unavailable, so no RustSec advisory scan was completed.
No production system, credential, customer data, deployment, or destructive database operation was used.
Dependency-license compatibility was not established by an automated license scanner.

assets: persisted download manifests and segment progress
download URLs, including potentially sensitive query strings
clipboard text inspected in process memory

trustBoundaries.boundary: remote HTTP server to shared Rust engine

implementedControls: completed-state gate for open and reveal

trustBoundaries.boundary: engine to Windows filesystem and shell adapters
Windows clipboard to application and webview
implementedControls: non-URL values not placed in download state

threats.scenario: A remote or URL-derived filename attempts traversal, an absolute path, an alternate data stream, or a Windows reserved device name.
threats.residualRisk: No behavioral test in this workstream covered symlink or reparse-point destination races; final canonical containment is not enforced after filesystem resolution.

threats.scenario: A server lies about Range support or segment length, causing corrupt assembly.
threats.residualRisk: Integrity is length-based only; there is no expected digest or validator binding, and a remote object changing between parallel requests may produce length-correct mixed content.

threats.scenario: Sensitive query parameters from download URLs are exposed in local manifests, clipboard offers, or diagnostics.
controlEvidence: unrelated non-URL clipboard text is not persisted
threats.residualRisk: The complete URL is persisted in DownloadManifest and emitted to the webview; reqwest errors written to stderr may include it. Retention and redaction are undefined.

threats.scenario: An untrusted server sends an unbounded body or stalls connections.
threats.residualRisk: Responses are accumulated into Vec buffers before writing, and the reqwest client has no explicit request timeout or maximum response size; a lying or missing length can exhaust memory or hold tasks indefinitely.

threats.scenario: Compromised webview content invokes file actions or downloads to an unintended path.
controlEvidence: open/reveal resolves a path from application state and requires completed status
threats.residualRisk: The destination is accepted as a webview-provided string rather than an opaque token issued by the folder picker; no generated capability file was found for least-privilege command/plugin scoping.

threats.scenario: A URL or redirect targets loopback, link-local, or private-network services.
controlEvidence: only HTTP and HTTPS URLs without userinfo are accepted
threats.residualRisk: Local/private addresses and redirect destinations are not restricted. This may be a deliberate desktop-client capability, but it must be documented and redirects must be revalidated if remote-only policy is intended.

findings.title: Network bodies are buffered without explicit size or time limits
findings.evidence: packages/download-engine/src/lib.rs collects every response stream into a Vec and the reqwest Client builder sets only redirect policy.
findings.recommendation: Stream each segment directly to a bounded file region, enforce per-request idle/overall timeouts, reject bodies exceeding the declared segment, and cap unknown-length downloads with an explicit policy.

findings.title: Length-only verification cannot detect a changing remote object
findings.evidence: Parallel requests are not bound to a common ETag or Last-Modified validator and final verification checks only byte length.
findings.recommendation: Capture a strong validator during probe, send If-Range on segment requests, reject inconsistent Content-Range totals/validators, and optionally verify a user/provider digest.

findings.title: Full URLs are retained and may appear in diagnostics
findings.evidence: DownloadManifest serializes url verbatim; clipboard-url-offer carries the verbatim clipboard URL; desktop errors are printed with Display formatting.
findings.recommendation: Document necessary URL retention, protect manifest access, remove URL query/fragment from UI and logs, use structured redacted errors, and provide lifecycle cleanup. Preserve the full URL only where resume requires it.

findings.title: Destination authority is not tied to a trusted picker result
findings.evidence: submit_url accepts an arbitrary destination string from the webview and create_dir_all uses it.
findings.recommendation: Issue an opaque destination grant from choose_destination, resolve/canonicalize it in Rust, and require subsequent commands to reference that grant.

findings.title: Reparse-point containment and replacement races are not defended
findings.evidence: Path checks reject ParentDir and sanitize the leaf, but do not canonicalize the destination or protect against links/reparse points and time-of-check/time-of-use replacement.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the chosen destination once, verify every created/opened path remains under it, and use no-follow/handle-based Windows filesystem operations where practical.

findings.title: GPL and third-party license distribution evidence is incomplete
findings.evidence: Both Rust packages declare GPL-3.0-only, but no root LICENSE was observed and no dependency-license report was available.
findings.recommendation: Within an authorized root-path workstream, add the exact GPL-3.0 text, generate a locked dependency license/SBOM report, review compatibility and notices, and gate distributable bundles on it.

findings.title: No automated advisory scan evidence
findings.evidence: Cargo.lock resolves dependencies and cargo tree completed, but cargo-audit is not installed in the verification environment.
findings.recommendation: Run cargo audit against the locked desktop dependency graph in CI and fail releases on unreviewed vulnerabilities; add cargo-deny for advisories, sources, bans, and licenses.

supplyChainReview.transport: download-engine uses reqwest 0.12 with default features disabled and rustls-tls enabled
supplyChainReview.duplicateVersionObservation: cargo tree --duplicates reports multiple versions in transitive build/runtime graphs; this is inspectable technical debt, not evidence of a vulnerability.
supplyChainReview.licenseDisposition: not ready for distribution; root GPL text and dependency-license evidence are missing
supplyChainReview.sourcePolicyDisposition: not established; cargo-deny or equivalent source allowlisting is recommended

privacyReview.clipboard: Polling is process-local every two seconds. Non-URL values fail shared URL validation and are not added to download state. Accepted URL values are emitted to the webview but do not automatically start a transfer.
privacyReview.persistence: Manifests persist full download URLs, output paths, status, total size, and segment offsets next to the output path. No unrelated clipboard value is intentionally persisted.
privacyReview.telemetry: No analytics or remote telemetry implementation was observed.
privacyReview.logging: A download failure is printed to stderr. Error redaction and retention are not defined.
privacyReview.dataMinimizationDisposition: partial; unrelated clipboard values are excluded, but URL query data and local paths require a documented retention/redaction policy

releaseGate.disposition: block distribution pending remediation or explicit risk acceptance

knownRisksAndLimitations: Pause/resume/cancel control correctness and UI/runtime accessibility are outside this security workstream's evidence and require behavioral verification.
A malicious local process with the user's filesystem privileges is outside the application's containment model.
Downloaded content is intentionally opened only after a user action, but antivirus/reputation scanning and code-signing policy are not implemented.
No claim is made that the current dependency graph is vulnerability-free or license-compatible.
The review did not alter shared business rules owned by the engine implementation workstreams.
